title: Coordinate Geometry
shortDescription: Distance, section formula, midpoint, centroid, area of triangle, slope and line conditions.
genZNote: Geometry with an address system: every point is (x, y), every formula is arithmetic.

sections.heading: Core Formulas
bullets: Distance between (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) = √[(x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²]; distance from origin = √(x² + y²).
Midpoint = ((x₁ + x₂)/2, (y₁ + y₂)/2); internal section m : n = ((mx₂ + nx₁)/(m + n), (my₂ + ny₁)/(m + n)).
Centroid of a triangle = ((x₁ + x₂ + x₃)/3, (y₁ + y₂ + y₃)/3).
Area of triangle = ½|x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂)|; collinear if area = 0.

sections.heading: Lines and Slopes
bullets: Slope m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁) = tan θ.
Equation forms: y = mx + c; point-slope y − y₁ = m(x − x₁); intercept form x/a + y/b = 1.
Parallel lines: m₁ = m₂; perpendicular: m₁m₂ = −1.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Coordinate geometry uses algebraic formulas for distance, division of segments, areas and line relationships.

commonTraps: Do not mix up x and y order.

sources.name: Standard quantitative aptitude reference (R.S. Aggarwal, Quantitative Aptitude)
